### Topic provenance

The topic came off the existing backlog rather than being invented:
`topic-what-it-infrastructure-means-for-small-business` (seeded by `scripts/seed-topics.ts`,
division `marketing`, status was `pending`). The script closes it out the way
`createPost.ts` does — `status: 'used'`, `usedAt`, `resultingPost` → the new post — so the
13B/13C generator can never write this topic a second time.

The other pending marketing topic, `topic-website-costing-customers` ("Five signs your
website is costing you customers"), was deliberately **not** used: it duplicates the
already-published `post-website-costing-customers`. It is still `pending` in the backlog
and should probably be retired by hand.

### Structure (both locales)

7 × `h2` sections, EN 1083 words / MK 1039 words:

1. Infrastructure is six things, not a server room — domain, DNS, hosting, email, files, backups
2. The failures are quiet, not dramatic — the four realistic failure modes at this size

5. What "good" looks like at ten people — the six-item target state
6. The audit you can run yourself this afternoon — six questions

Every factual claim about what Vertex does is taken from

## `scripts/publish-post-it-infrastructure.ts`

New one-off script, same family as `seed-blog.ts` / `seed-topics.ts`.

- **Env loading:** tries `.env.local`, then falls back to `env.local`. On this machine
  the values live in **`env.local`** (no leading dot) — which is also why the Sanity-backed
  blog is empty on a local `next dev`/`next start`: Next only auto-loads `.env.local`,
  so the local server has no `NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_PROJECT_ID` and `isSanityConfigured`
  is false. The existing seed scripts, which load `.env.local` only, cannot run as
  documented on this machine either.
- **Idempotent:** fixed `_id` + `createOrReplace`; re-runs reuse the already-uploaded
  featured image instead of pushing a duplicate into the media library, and preserve the
  original `publishedAt` so an edit does not shuffle the post to the top of the listing.
- **Guards:** aborts if the slug is owned by a different document, or if `author-lazar`
  is missing from the dataset.
- **Quality gates:** imports the real `validateDraft()` from
  `src/lib/contentGenerator/validateDraft.ts` and runs the hand-written copy through the
  exact gates Claude's output has to pass — word counts, ≥2 `h2` per locale, excerpt
  60–300 chars, 3–5 tags, read time 3–15, banned marketing phrases. All pass.
- **Portable Text:** inline `mdToPortableText()` with the same contract as `seed-blog.ts`,
  restricted to what `localizedPortableText` actually allows (`normal` + `h2`, `bullet`
  lists, `strong`, `link`).
- **Post-publish:** POSTs `/api/revalidate` with `x-revalidate-secret`, `{tag:'blog', slug}`.
  Targets `siteConfig.url` by default (override with `REVALIDATE_TARGET_URL`) because
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` in `env.local` is `http://localhost:3000` — the generator's own
  revalidate step therefore only ever hits localhost from this machine.

Flags: `--check` (validate, no writes) · `--draft` (write as draft) · `--no-revalidate`.

# Part 2 — Featured-image backfill on the three original posts

Follow-up request: "add photos to the existing 3 blogs as well."

`seed-blog.ts` migrated the three mock posts before Phase 13B existed, so none of
them ever had a `featuredImage`. They were the only posts on the site without one.

## What was done

`scripts/backfill-blog-images.ts` uploads one hand-picked Pexels photo per post and
`.patch()`es **only** the `featuredImage` field — deliberately not `createOrReplace`,
since these are documents the script did not author.

| Post | Division | Pexels | Asset | Photographer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `post-workflow-overhaul` | consulting | 6804093 | `image-5d12f42839a6578882b968ba46790c27b7c753af-1880x1253-jpg` | cottonbro studio |
| `post-website-costing-customers` | marketing | 5839461 | `image-d10982b66cbdea4bc52d4aee10795bed60c56301-1880x1253-jpg` | Magnetme |
| `post-ai-tools-2026` | shared | 7679173 | `image-e92e038b9d61fcd4c762a714aa07fca49f2d4306-1880x1254-jpg` | Mikhail Nilov |

Photos were chosen by eye from 52 candidates across 7 search queries, not taken from
`searchPexelsPhoto()`'s first hit:

- **Workflow post** — a kanban board chalked on dark brick (ICE BOX / In progress /
  Emergency / Testing / Complete). Literally a workflow rather than generic meeting
  stock, and the dark frame suits the consulting division's dark theme.
- **Website post** — someone holding a phone up beside the same site open on a laptop.
  That is exactly the "open your own site on your phone right now" test the post asks
  the reader to run.
- **AI post** — a desk with laptop, printed documents, notebook and phone. The post's
  strongest use case is document processing, so paperwork beats a robot; also avoids
  dating the post with a specific model or UI.

**Pinned by photo ID, not by query.** The script calls `GET /v1/photos/{id}` rather than
searching, so a re-run can never silently swap in whatever Pexels currently ranks first.
Idempotent: posts that already have an image are skipped (`--force` overrides);
`--dry-run` reports without writing.

## Verified in production

- All four posts now render a card image on `/en/blog`; alt text correct in both locales.
- All four assets serve through `/_next/image` → **200**, 28–43 KB at `w=828`.
- `BlogPosting` JSON-LD `image` on each of the three now points at the real
  `cdn.sanity.io` asset instead of falling back to the generic `/opengraph-image`.
- The listing page picked the change up within a minute of the `/api/revalidate` flush;
  the three individual post pages lagged it by a couple of minutes.

## Template gaps this surfaced (fixed in Part 3 below)

Attaching the images exposed two pre-existing limitations in the blog **template**,
affecting all four posts equally including the new one:

1. **The article page never renders the featured image.** `BlogPostClient.tsx` reads
   `post.featuredImage?.url` at line 68 for one purpose only — the `image` array in the
   `BlogPosting` JSON-LD. There is no hero `<Image>` anywhere in the article body. The
   photos are therefore visible on the listing/related cards and to crawlers, but a
   reader who opens a post sees no photo.
2. **`og:image` ignores the featured image.** `generateMetadata` in
   `blog/[slug]/page.tsx` calls `generatePageMetadata({title, description, path, locale})`
   with no image argument, so every post shares the site-wide `/opengraph-image`. Sharing
   any post to Facebook/LinkedIn shows the generic Vertex card rather than the post photo
   — which also undercuts the 13C social-posting pipeline.

Both were then approved and fixed — see Part 3.

# Part 3 — Blog template: hero image + real social cards

Follow-up: "yes fix both." Two code changes, both in `blog/[slug]/`.

## 1. Hero image on the article page — `BlogPostClient.tsx`

`post.featuredImage` was read at one place only (the `image` array of the `BlogPosting`
JSON-LD). Nothing rendered it, so every post page was photoless no matter what the CMS held.

Now renders a `<figure>` at the top of the content Section, above the prose:

| Decision | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Measure | `max-w-3xl` (768px) | Matches the **header** block (title/excerpt/author), not the narrower `prose-blog` text column (~578px). Left edges align with everything; the image reads as a deliberate full-column element rather than a floating banner. |
| Ratio | `aspect-video` | The four assets range 3:2 to 4:3. A fixed ratio makes every post present identically, and matches `BlogCard`. |
| Chrome | `rounded-[12px]` + `border-[var(--division-border)]` on `--division-card` | Same language as BlogCard. Both tokens, so light/dark track automatically — verified `#404040` dark / `#e3e7ec` light. |
| Loading | `priority`, LQIP `placeholder="blur"` | At this position it is the LCP element. `lqip` is present on all five assets. |
| Alt | `featuredImage.alt?.[locale] ?? post.title` | The field is optional in the schema; a redundant alt beats an empty one. Same fallback BlogCard uses. |

Guarded on `post.featuredImage`, so a post without one renders exactly as before.

## 2. Real social cards — `blog/[slug]/page.tsx`

`generateMetadata` called `generatePageMetadata({title, description, path, locale})` with no
image, so every post's `og:image` was the site-wide `/opengraph-image`. Sharing any post
anywhere showed generic Vertex branding — and that is the card the 13C social pipeline leans on.

`generatePageMetadata` already accepted an `image` option (added for the project
screenshots), so this is just feeding it:

```
`${post.featuredImage.url}?w=1200&h=630&fit=crop&crop=entropy&fm=jpg&q=80`
```

- Sanity's CDN does the 1.91:1 crop, so assets can stay whatever shape they were uploaded at.
- `crop=entropy` picks the busiest region instead of blindly centring.
- `fm=jpg` because LinkedIn and some chat clients still refuse WebP.
- Verified the URL returns a genuine **1200x630 JPEG, 78 KB**.
- No featured image → `image: null` → unchanged site-wide fallback.

## Verification

Local verification needed real Sanity env, and running a second server in the repo would have
fought the other session's `next start` (AGENTS.md forbids it). So: a throwaway copy at
`/home/user/.cache/vertex-verify` — source copied, `node_modules` **hardlinked** (`cp -al`;
/tmp is tmpfs and 1.4 GB would not fit, and Turbopack rejects a `node_modules` symlink
pointing outside the project root), `env.local` copied in as `.env.local`, `next dev -p 3005`.
Removed afterwards; the project's own `node_modules` verified intact.

- All **8** post/locale variants render exactly one `<figure>` and a `cdn.sanity.io` `og:image`.
- Geometry desktop: 768x432, ratio 1.778, 48px gap to prose, order title → image → prose.
- Geometry mobile (375): 343x193, ratio 1.778, left-aligned with prose, **no** horizontal overflow.
- Themes: border/background resolve from `--division-*` tokens in both.
- MK: `alt` and `og:image:alt` both carry the Macedonian string.
- Blur placeholder present in server HTML (the SVG-filter data-URI Next emits), removed once loaded.
- **Imageless fallback exercised** by temporarily forcing `featuredImage` to null in the
  throwaway copy: no `<figure>`, `og:image` and JSON-LD both fall back to `/opengraph-image`,
  page otherwise identical. No console errors, clean dev log.

`tsc --noEmit` and `npm run lint` clean.
